That `ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/test -f /etc/kata/kata.env` parks the unit until the env file arrives, that `EnvironmentFile=-` keeps an absent file non-fatal, and that `Restart=on-failure` plus systemd's start-rate limit behave as the design assumes, cannot be exercised without systemd. [structural false-green: sandbox could not execute it against the target]

5 — plan-defect: leg (f) expects the sheet-driven green run's close message to be `adopted in wave 1 (PASS)`, but M6 specifies `adopted in wave <n> (<its reviewVerdict>)`. A `done` row's reviewVerdict is `clean` (round 1) or `fixed` (round 2) — never `PASS`, which is the referee's own verdict string and never reaches the row. No implementation can satisfy both. I implemented M6 literally, so the close message reads `adopted in wave 1 (clean)` on a first-round-clean run; the rest of leg (f) (reason, evidence shape, idempotencyKey `sim:T1:close`, the wontfix shapes, the left-open wave-2 task) is satisfied as written.

6 — plan-defect: leg (d) says the issues endpoint fails `with STUB_KATA_ISSUES_EXIT=22 from the second transition on` while the Context sketches a plain `exit ${STUB_KATA_ISSUES_EXIT:-0}` arm. One boot is one process with one environment, so a static knob cannot fail only from the second transition, and a static 22 would mean no kata.jsonl ever exists — leg (d)'s `the file's four lines are unchanged` could not hold. The rig's issues arm therefore counts its calls and applies the exit code from its `STUB_KATA_ISSUES_EXIT_FROM`-th call on, defaulting to 2, with `STUB_KATA_ISSUES_EXIT_FROM=1` available to fail every call. This is a deviation from the Context's literal stub sketch; a peer exam written against that sketch and expecting every call to fail must set `STUB_KATA_ISSUES_EXIT_FROM=1`.
